headline: ENZO: Open-source AI platform runs 300+ models locally on your own keys & infrastructure
summary: ENZO offers a full-fledged AI workspace with agents and skills, allowing users to chat with over 300 models, generate code, and run research entirely on their own infrastructure using their API keys, with no accounts or subscriptions.
details: ENZO is an open-source, self-hosted AI platform designed for privacy and control. It allows users to chat with over 300 models, build agents, generate code, and conduct research, all running on their own infrastructure using their API keys. There are no ENZO accounts, usage meters, or subscriptions.

Installation is streamlined via Docker Desktop, requiring no database server or complex setup. Provider keys are saved encrypted in the browser's passphrase-protected vault, ensuring they never touch the server. The first validated key claims the instance, unlocking server-side features like agents and memory.

The platform supports agents that can write their own operating manuals and integrate with tools like Gmail and Calendar. Projects, learned skills, and agent memory are stored in named Docker volumes, ensuring data persistence across upgrades and restarts.

For those preferring not to self-host, ENZO offers a live demo on enzo-hub.duckdns.org and a Colab notebook setup. The Colab option runs on Google's hardware but guarantees that user model keys remain private and are wiped when the session ends.

Unlike most 'AI workspaces' that hold user keys, meter usage, or require subscriptions, ENZO operates on a 'bring your own key' model. This ensures direct payment to providers without any intermediary cuts, maximizing user control and privacy.

System requirements include Docker Desktop for Mac or Windows with WSL 2, allocating at least 4 GB RAM. The full threat model is documented for transparency, detailing how each security claim is implemented in the code.
